summary: Sixteen misses, ten of them near-coin-flip calls that landed the wrong way (five were one correlated fall in the 10-year yield). The data-gathering gaps seen (in-window price lows, an unopened survey) are already covered by current checklist items, so no items are added.

misses.note: 0.60 on a 4bp gap over 4 trading days was a fair random-walk number; the yield slipped to 5.22 vs a 5.24 threshold.
Same setup as the Oct 8 question; the strict 'above' threshold of 5.24 was met only as a tie (5.24), which resolves No.
Near-coin-flip at 0.56 with a small momentum tilt; the yield fell to 5.21 from 5.28 after the weak payrolls, a fall inside one standard deviation.
0.55 on a threshold at the current level with CPI on the day; the yield ended 5.19, part of the same correlated drop as the other rate misses.
0.55 with the level near the threshold and six trading days left; the yield fell to 5.10, again the same drop, not a data error.
Touch odds near 55% for a 4% dip in 65 hours were reasonable; the low stayed above the level, and the checklist's price-source and distance items were followed.
0.30 for a gated model going public within days was reasonable given no date; it opened before the deadline, and the packet holds no research record showing a better signal.
Leaned on incumbency and a government-aligned poll over independent polls showing the student list ahead, so the 0.35 was too low.
Did not find the Binance 1-minute lows for the days of the window already elapsed (1 of 5 sources checked); the existing price-touch item asks for exactly that.
Reasoned from first-round shares and where the minor-candidate votes would go, with no runoff polls or past first-round-to-runoff swings, and gave the trailing candidate 0.35.
Gave the party 0.33 against a 2-4 seat poll deficit and flagged its history of beating final polls; it did beat them.
Own base-effect and holiday arithmetic gave 2.8% against the bank's 3.3% full-year forecast implying about 3.0% for H2; the bucket 3.0-3.4 held the result.
The first print came in at exactly 194,000, and a tie resolves No under the strict 'above'; 0.63 for a lean above the latest print was reasonable.
Consensus came only from a search summary and no page opened (fetch refused by the proxy, 0 of 4 sources checked), so the lean to a hike rested on an unverified survey.
Research was thorough (8 of 8 sources checked) and put 0.25 on a downward revision of the advance estimate; the revision came.
0.8 on a leaderboard position from a five-day-old snapshot, with the rank spreads of the second and third labs overlapping (2-4) and eight days to the check.
